question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=180$ and $p=0.45.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =180\cdot 0.45 \\  & =81 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =180\cdot (1-0.45) \\  & =99 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(180)(0.45)=81
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(180)(0.45)(1-0.45)=44.55.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(81,44.55).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=85).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=85)≈P(84.5\le Y\le 85.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(84.5\le Y\le 85.5) & =P(\frac{84.5-81}{\sqrt{44.55}}\le Z\le \frac{85.5-81}{\sqrt{44.55}}) \\  & ≈P(0.52\le Z\le 0.67) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.67)-P(Z<0.52) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.67)-P(Z\le 0.52) \\  & =Φ(0.67)-Φ(0.52) \\  & =0.7486-0.6985 \\  & =0.0501\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=85)≈0.050.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0499.$
